notes: Assertion '创建了 changes/CHG-001/ 目录结构' passes 100% in both configurations — non-discriminating, as both approaches create a CHG-001 directory. Consider removing or making it more specific.
All other assertions are highly discriminating: they pass 100% with skill and fail 100% without skill. The skill's three-level progressive model (spec/plan/tasks/checklist) is the key differentiator.

Without-skill runs consistently produce a single change.md or ad-hoc numbered files instead of the structured 4-doc model. Content quality is often good (e.g., eval-2 without_skill has detailed code diffs), but the structure doesn't match the spec/plan/tasks/checklist convention.
Skill adds ~13s average execution time (43.7s vs 30.3s) but improves pass rate by 89 percentage points (100% vs 11%). The time overhead comes from reading the skill and creating 4 separate documents.

Zero variance in with_skill pass rate (100% ± 0%) across all 3 evals indicates consistent skill performance regardless of change complexity (simple feature change vs medium refactor vs large new feature).
Eval-3 (RBAC) shows the largest time delta (50s vs 37s) — the skill's impact analysis protocol adds most value on complex changes covering multiple dimensions (docs+code+designs).
The without_skill approach for eval-3 produced 9 documents (more than with_skill's 4), but none matched the required format — suggesting the skill's value is in structural guidance, not quantity.
